label: Salt formation 10ns: does history fraction drift (first-half fraction minus second-half fraction) add on top of the full fraction?
series: K2 (what the guidance is, not where it is)

conditions_definition.base: K15 expanded conditions: train 58 proteins (orig 4 + 54 additions), test 30 proteins (orig 2 + 28 additions), frozen split from K15 split.json, origin frame 10 (1 ns), history frames 0-10 (100 ps spacing), HistGBM (120 iters, lr 0.075, 31 leaves, min_samples_leaf 15, L2 0.02, seed 42) refit per condition, distance = minimum over charged heavy-atom pairs, bound 4.0 A, candidates = pairs NOT salt-bridged at the origin frame.
conditions_definition.base_hist_D6: static + 6 history statistics (first, mean, std, min, last-first, fraction <= bound) over frames 0-10
conditions_definition.drift_only: static + drift only (fraction over frames [0..4] minus fraction over frames [6..10])
conditions_definition.frac_full: static + fraction over frames [0..10] (fraction of frames with min distance <= 4.0 A)
conditions_definition.frac_both_halves: static + first-half fraction and second-half fraction (K2-140 reference)

base_reproduction.reference: K15 saltbridge_expansion results.json full/ (10 ns: static 0.2034, full hist6 0.2627, gain +0.0594); full fraction 0.2326 from K2-140 (same conditions, 10 ns)

caution: Base gain is small (+0.0594) and the test set is small (1,170 candidates, 131 positives), so AUPRC differences near the +0.01 line are noisy. Per-protein candidate counts average ~39, so per-protein AUPRCs are noisy.
verdict: 漂いは足しにならない
